newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan questions suspected Chinese illegal aliens.
newsitem.headline: Japan questions suspected Chinese illegal aliens.

text.p: Police in southern Japan were questioning 49 people who appear to be Chinese on suspicion of illegal entry, a police spokesman said on Thursday.
"We are questioning 41 men and eight women who were reported to have landed around noon on an uninhabited island 100 km (70 miles) west of Nagasaki," a Nagasaki Prefectural Police spokesman said.
"They appear to be Chinese and we suspect they illegally entered the country," he added.
Local fishermen reported seeing the group on one of the Goto group of islets around noon (0300 GMT), the spokesman said.

Japan has been bracing itself for a flood of illegals since the number of illegal immigrants hauled in by navy and police officials by April topped 500, more than the total number of Chinese illegals caught in all of last year.

The spokesman said police have had to resort to asking for the public's help as Nagasaki Prefecture's long, rugged coast makes it particularly prone to illegal immigration despite increased navy patrols.
Nagasaki lies just across the East China Sea from China.

"There are many landings in these parts although the maritime authorities have upped the number of patrols. We're asking locals to report to us if they spot any suspicious foreigners and we're also publicising the problem as widely as we can," he said.
Japan's parliament in April boosted the maximum jail term for those who help illegal immigrants enter Japan from 18 months to 10 years imprisonment in an effort to deter the influx.
